global_metadata.project_title: Hazard Waste Detection Using AI and IoT

ai_context: A mobile robot for hazardous waste detection. ESP32 (NodeMCU ESP32S) drives four 12V DC encoder motors through two L298N drivers, powered by a 12V Li-ion pack via an XT60 power distribution board. An ESP32-CAM streams live video; an ESP8266 NodeMCU controls a pan-tilt servo mount (SG90) and a 0.96in I2C OLED status display. A Flask server receives the stream, runs a custom-trained YOLOv11 model (Ultralytics, OpenCV) to detect hazards such as chemical containers, batteries, plastic waste, fire and gas leaks, and serves a web dashboard (HTML/CSS/JS) with gamepad-style movement controls, camera controls, live stream, status and server logs. Modules talk over UDP broadcast on Wi-Fi. Firmware written with PlatformIO (Arduino framework). Testing: unit tests per module (motor control, camera streaming, YOLO detection, UDP communication, power/voltage), integration testing; observed 1-2 s stream latency at high resolution. Limitations: only visually apparent hazards, Wi-Fi dependency, manual navigation, battery life, lighting sensitivity. Future: gas sensors, SLAM navigation, LoRa/4G, solar charging, edge inference, real-time alerts, mobile app. Papers: ChemiRover - Integrated IoT and ML for Hazardous Area Monitoring (Aayush Gadiya; Harsh Badagandi; Mayank Ahuja; Anil Kadu, 2024); Remote Monitoring of Hazardous Environment at Mining Sites Using LoRa Network (Asfar H. Siddiqui; Anup Ranade; Akshaykumar Meshram; Vinod Waiker, 2024); Garbage Classification using Machine Learning to Aid Recycling (Harsh Sanjay Pandita; Vidhi Vaidya; Mayur Doifode; Prasenjit Bhavthankar; Anantalakshmi Venkatesh, 2022).
